title: Security Trading Policy

tiers.name: Catapult Team Members and Adhering Contractors
tiers.description: Every director, officer or employee of Catapult or its subsidiaries (Catapult Team Member) and every contractor, consultant or employee of a contractor who has agreed to comply with Catapult's policies generally or this policy specifically (Adhering Contractor). All may deal outside Blackout Periods without inside information; only margin loans/security arrangements and unvested hedging are separately restricted for this whole group.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: Chairman, Directors (other than the Chairman), the CEO, CEO Direct Reports, the Company Secretary, the CFO, and other Finance Department/senior staff or executive assistants nominated under section 7.2. Must obtain Pre-Clearance from named Designated Approvers before any Dealing, in addition to the Blackout Period restriction.

tiers.name: Related Parties/Associates
tiers.description: A parent, spouse, de facto spouse, son or daughter of a Catapult Team Member or Adhering Contractor, and any company, trust or other entity such persons (alone or together) control. The policy's restrictions and the pre-clearance/exceptional-circumstances application (made 'by me, my Related Parties or Associates') extend to dealings by this group.

definitions.hedging_definition: transactions in associated products that operate to limit the economic risk of Catapult Securities over unvested entitlements

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may determine any other period as a Blackout Period, which may apply to one or more Catapult Team Members or Adhering Contractors, or groups of them; the policy does not state whether such additional Blackout Periods are kept confidential.

rules.detail: No express derivatives rule for non-Designated Persons. Catapult Securities includes derivatives (including options) with no venue limit, and Dealing includes granting, acquiring, disposing, exercising or discharging any option or other right over Securities, so an OTC put/call is a Dealing. For this tier it only needs to occur outside a Blackout Period and without Inside Information; no clearance is required.
rules.evidence: any derivatives, including but not limited to, options in respect of any of the securities in paragraph (a) above.

rules.detail: For Designated Persons the same OTC derivative Dealing additionally requires Pre-Clearance from all of that person's Designated Approvers before dealing, on top of the Blackout Period restriction.
rules.evidence: Each Designated Person may only Deal in Catapult Securities if ... prior to their Dealing, they receive Pre-Clearance, which is approval in advance from all of their Designated Approvers

rules.detail: Absolute ban on transactions in associated products limiting the economic risk of Catapult Securities over unvested entitlements, applying to all Team Members and Adhering Contractors with no clearance route.
rules.evidence: Catapult prohibits Catapult Team Members and Adhering Contractors from entering into transactions in associated products that operate to limit the economic risk of Catapult Securities over unvested entitlements.

rules.detail: Hedging of vested holdings is not separately named; it is caught only as an ordinary Dealing (option/derivative) requiring compliance with Blackout Periods and the insider trading prohibition, with no clearance for this tier.
rules.evidence: the grant, acceptance, acquisition, disposal, exercise or discharge of any option or other right or obligation to acquire or dispose of any Catapult Securities.

rules.detail: A Designated Person hedging vested holdings must obtain Pre-Clearance from their Designated Approvers and deal outside Blackout Periods; the section 10 unvested ban does not apply once vested.
rules.evidence: prior to their Dealing, they receive Pre-Clearance, which is approval in advance from all of their Designated Approvers in accordance with this section 7.

rules.detail: Monetisation (e.g. a prepaid forward) is not named; it is caught as an agreement to dispose of Catapult Securities, so it is a Dealing needing only Blackout Period and inside information compliance for this tier.
rules.evidence: entering into any agreement to acquire or dispose of any Catapult Securities

rules.detail: For a Designated Person the same monetisation agreement additionally requires Pre-Clearance from their Designated Approvers.
rules.evidence: prior to their Dealing, they receive Pre-Clearance, which is approval in advance from all of their Designated Approvers

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the policy or the Dealing definition.
Securities lending is not named and is not listed in the Dealing definition.
CFDs are not named. As a derivative in respect of Catapult Securities they fall within the Dealing definition, requiring only Blackout Period and inside information compliance for this tier.
rules.evidence: Catapult Securities means: ... any derivatives, including but not limited to, options in respect of any of the securities

rules.detail: A Designated Person dealing in a CFD over Catapult Securities requires Pre-Clearance from their Designated Approvers.
rules.evidence: Each Designated Person may only Deal in Catapult Securities if ... they receive Pre-Clearance

rules.detail: Applies to all Catapult Team Members and Adhering Contractors, not only Designated Persons: a margin loan requires prior written approval of the Designated Approvers, grantable subject to any conditions. The policy does not identify who the 'Designated Approvers' are for a person who is not a Designated Person under section 7.2.
rules.evidence: Catapult Team Members and Adhering Contractors may only enter into a margin loan or other security arrangement in respect of Catapult Securities with the prior written approval of the Designated Approvers

rules.detail: Any 'other security arrangement' (charge, lien or pledge) over Catapult Securities, not just margin loans, requires prior written approval of the Designated Approvers.
rules.evidence: or other security arrangement in respect of Catapult Securities with the prior written approval of the Designated Approvers

rules.detail: No blanket prohibition: any secured financing arrangement in respect of Catapult Securities is permitted with prior written approval of the Designated Approvers, and that approval may be made conditional on Catapult disclosing to ASX the existence of the arrangement and terms such as trigger points or the financier's right to sell unilaterally.
rules.evidence: Any approval by the Designated Approvers may be subject to the condition that Catapult be permitted to disclose to the ASX the existence of the margin loan or security arrangement, and, where Catapult considers appropriate, any relevant terms such as the trigger points or right of the financier to sell unilaterally.

rules.detail: No minimum holding period, LIFO rule or intention-based short-term dealing restriction is stated anywhere in the policy.

exceptions.evidence: transfers of Catapult Securities that result in no change to the beneficial interest in the Catapult Securities;
transfers of Catapult Securities between a Catapult Team Member or an Adhering Contractor and their Related Parties;
transfers of Catapult Securities by a Catapult Team Member or an Adhering Contractor to their superannuation fund;

exceptions.approver: other trustees or independent investment managers
exceptions.evidence: where a Catapult Team Member or an Adhering Contractor is a trustee, Trading in the Catapult Securities by the relevant trust, provided that the Catapult Team Member or Adhering Contractor is not a beneficiary of that trust and any decision to Trade during a Blackout Period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently
undertakings to accept, the acceptance of, or disposal of, Catapult Securities arising from a takeover offer, scheme of arrangement or equal access buy-back;

Trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the holders of Catapult Securities, such as a rights issue, security purchase plan, dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back
a disposal of Catapult Securities that is the result of a secured lender or financier exercising their rights under a loan agreement;

an acquisition or disposal of Catapult Securities under a pre-determined investment or divestment plan for which prior written approval has been provided by the Designated Approver and where ... the plan does not permit the Catapult Team Member or Adhering Contractor to exercise any discretion over how, when, or whether to acquire or dispose of Catapult Securities
an acquisition of Catapult Securities under an employee incentive scheme.
whether the Applicant is suffering severe financial hardship;
whether the Applicant is required by a court order or a court-enforceable undertaking or other legal or regulatory requirement to transfer, or accept a transfer of, Catapult Securities;
whether the Applicant's circumstances are otherwise exceptional to warrant the grant of approval to Deal in Catapult Securities during the Blackout Period.

financing_disclosure: All Catapult Team Members and Adhering Contractors; trigger: entering into a margin loan or other security arrangement, as a condition the Designated Approvers may impose on granting approval; to: ASX (via Catapult); deadline: not specified.

external_documents: Catapult employee incentive plans (referenced in clause 1.4 as an additional, potentially more restrictive, source of dealing restrictions)
exemption_authority: Designated Approvers may refuse or grant Pre-Clearance, section 9 financing approvals, and Exceptional-Circumstances Blackout Period approvals, each in their absolute discretion and subject to any conditions they consider necessary (7.4, 8.2, 9.1). Exceptional Circumstances during a Blackout Period may be granted for severe financial hardship, court order/legal requirement, or other exceptional circumstances (8.3). No general waiver of the insider trading prohibition exists.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Catapult Securities that is the result of a secured lender or financier exercising their rights under a loan agreement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares on default is expressly carved out of the policy's Dealing restrictions, so it is not blocked by a Blackout Period, Pre-Clearance failure, or possession of Inside Information by the executive.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any approval by the Designated Approvers may be subject to the condition that Catapult be permitted to disclose to the ASX the existence of the margin loan or security arrangement, and ... any relevant terms such as the trigger points or right of the financier to sell unilaterally.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank should expect the loan secured on the collared shares, and its trigger/enforcement terms, may be required to be disclosed publicly as a condition of Catapult's approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Catapult Team Members and Adhering Contractors may only enter into a margin loan or other security arrangement in respect of Catapult Securities with the prior written approval of the Designated Approvers
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Section 9.1's approval requirement applies to every Team Member/Contractor, but 'Designated Approvers' is only defined (7.2) for people who are themselves Designated Persons, leaving unclear who approves a financing arrangement for an executive who is not a Designated Person; the bank should have this confirmed before relying on the approval process.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Catapult prohibits Catapult Team Members and Adhering Contractors from entering into transactions in associated products that operate to limit the economic risk of Catapult Securities over unvested entitlements.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar can only be written over Catapult Securities that have already vested; unvested awards cannot be the reference security under any approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company Secretary may, from time to time, establish, amend and remove rules to provide prospective approval to Dealings in Catapult Securities during permitted periods by one or more Designated Persons ... (the Prospective Rules)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If a Prospective Rule were established for a Designated Person, the derivative legs of a collar could in principle be pre-approved on a standing basis rather than needing case-by-case Pre-Clearance, though this would need to be arranged with the Company Secretary/Chairman.

bespoke_clauses.clause: this policy applies, for example, to Dealings in Catapult Securities by a Catapult Team Member's spouse ... I request the Designated Approvers' approval for the following proposed transaction to be undertaken by me, my Related Parties or Associates
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or its financing through a spouse, family trust or controlled entity does not avoid the Pre-Clearance or section 9 financing approval requirements.

summary: A funded collar is achievable but requires two separate approvals to run in parallel. The OTC put and call are Dealings caught only via the Catapult Securities/Dealing definitions (no express derivatives rule); a Designated Person needs Pre-Clearance from their specific Designated Approvers and must deal outside Blackout Periods, while a non-Designated employee needs no clearance for the derivative legs, only compliance with Blackout Periods and the insider trading prohibition. The loan secured on the collared shares is expressly permitted, not banned, under section 9 as a 'margin loan or other security arrangement', but requires prior written approval of the Designated Approvers, and Catapult may condition that approval on disclosing the arrangement's existence and trigger terms to ASX; the policy does not say who approves this for an employee who is not themselves a Designated Person. The collar cannot be written over unvested entitlements, only vested Catapult Securities, since limiting the economic risk of unvested holdings is absolutely prohibited. A lender's enforcement sale on default is expressly excluded from the policy's Dealing restrictions, so forced liquidation is not blocked by a Blackout Period or lack of clearance. There is no minimum shareholding requirement or short-term dealing rule to otherwise constrain the structure.
